title: Minimax Estimation of Oracle Policy Gain under a Sparse Treatment Budget
banked_reason: kernel_substituted@thm:matched-frontier: the proposed matched growing-alphabet scarce-capacity frontier is not delivered; the proved result leaves a logarithmic lower-to-upper gap for d>=3.
gap_reasons: The proposed matched growing-alphabet scarce-capacity frontier is not delivered: this theorem explicitly leaves a logarithmic lower-to-upper gap for d≥3, so it is a useful bracket rather than the promised sharp rate.
The sharper growing-alphabet upper bound Cε ρ_{n,d,b} is not asserted.
proof_attempt_summary: The run pursued a matched all-procedure scarce-capacity minimax rate for growing d. It derived sound lower and upper bounds, but the upper bound remains up to a logarithmic factor above the lower bound for d≥3; the observable offset estimator needed to close this gap was not constructed. The field-floor review graded the delivered bracket incremental and the D0.5 decision referee identified kernel substitution in the matched-frontier headline.
tldr: When treatment can reach only fraction \(b\), the gain from the oracle randomized policy is bounded by \(b\), but its threshold is selected using unknown cell masses and may have a mass-one tie. A total map from every observed table, including null cells, defines the dual gain without hidden conditional-mean conventions. The proved result is the all-procedure lower-to-upper bracket for \(d\ge3\), with lower scale \(\min\{b^2,bd/[n\log(ed)]\}\) and total-observable upper \(\min\{b^2,bd/n,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\); fully specified same-class boundary laws give \(\min\{b^2,b/n\}\) for \(d=2\) and \(b^2/n\) for \(d=1\). A legal rare-block reduction supplies the logarithmic lower scale only where a rare pair and filler cell exist. The unresolved question asks whether a pilot-local polynomial hinge construction can satisfy two offset dual inequalities and close the logarithmic gap, or whether the proposed sharper frontier must be corrected.
gap: The accepted full-curve theorem has global risk \(\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\), but its lower construction is fixed at half capacity. Regular constrained-value inference assumes continuous zero-mass cutoffs, while large-alphabet polynomial methods treat fixed cusps rather than a threshold chosen from unknown masses.
fill: A total observed-table map fixes null-cell and zero-arm conventions and identifies the dual gain. For \(d\ge3\), a fully specified joint rare-subpopulation law yields the legal same-class converse; fully specified one-cell and two-cell joint laws cover the boundary dimensions. A capacity-sensitive Hellinger modulus and a declared selector with the clipped accepted curve estimator yield an explicit total-observable provisional upper bracket. An offset threshold-process certificate targets the remaining logarithmic upper improvement without assuming a small weak upper tail.
